To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the composite test of focal liver defects, elevated CEA, and hepatomegally or elevated alkaline phosphatases has a predictive value of about 90% and an overall diagnostic accuracy of about 90%.

liver scan, CEA assay and alkaline phosphatases can be used to identify patients with hepatic metastases from GI malignancies, with high sensitivity and specificity, and that these tests can be combined to form a composite test that has an even higher sensitivity and specificity.

the CEA test is a useful adjunct to liver scan, but not a replacement for it, and that the composite test, which includes both the CEA and the scintigraphic results, provides a more accurate estimate of the probability that a patient has liver metastases than does the liver scan alone.

the development of a composite test for the detection of hepatic metastasis from GI cancers.
the use of CEA as an adjunct to the radionuclide liver scan in the assessment of patients with GI malignancies.
a new method of liver scanning and with the use of CEA and other liver enzymes in conjunction with liver scanning in the diagnosis of liver metastases in patients with GI malignancies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CEA assay is not a substitute for liver scan, but it is an important adjunct to the scan, and it is an essential part of the diagnostic work-up of GI cancer patients.

the liver scan is a useful and accurate test for the detection of metastases in the liver, and that it should be employed in conjunction with other tests in a composite fashion to achieve maximum accuracy.
the combination of CEA and liver scan is more accurate than liver scan alone, and that CEA is a useful adjunct to liver scan for detecting liver metastases from GI cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the liver scan is an excellent test for the detection of metastases in the liver from GI cancer, and that the CEA assay can be used to increase the accuracy of the liver scan in the absence of a focal defect.
the combination of liver scan and CEA assay provides a highly reliable means to detect hepatic metastases in the patient with GI cancer.
CEA and liver scan should be considered complementary rather than competitive in the evaluation of liver metastases.

the use of a composite test, in which the scintiscan and the serum CEA level are combined with clinical and laboratory findings, may be helpful for improving accuracy in the detection of hepatic metastasis from primary digestive-tract malignancies.
the use of the carcinoembryogenic antigen assay as a complementary test to liver scanning can improve the detection rate of hepatic metastasis in GI malignancy.
